question:
A 75-year-old woman presents to the emergency department with a 2-week history of worsening
shortness of breath, swelling in her lower extremities, and a 3-kg (6.6-lb) weight gain. Chest
auscultation reveals crackles, and cardiac examination detects a dull, low-pitched early diastolic sound
at the 5th left intercostal space, which becomes more pronounced in the left lateral decubitus position
during end-expiration. What is the most likely cause of these auscultatory findings? Answer Choices:
(A) Increased left ventricular end-systolic volume (B) Left atrial enlargement (C) Impaired mitral valve
closure (D) Decreased cardiac output (E) Increased left atrial pressure (F) Decreased left-ventricular
filling pressure (G) Decreased left myocardial compliance (H) Increased pulmonary capillary wedge
pressure (I) Decreased stroke volume (J) Impaired diastolic relaxation
 A. Decreased left-ventricular filling pressure
B. Impaired mitral valve closure
C. Decreased left myocardial compliance
D. Impaired diastolic relaxation
E. Decreased stroke volume
F. Increased left ventricular end-systolic volume
G. Decreased cardiac output

H. Left atrial enlargement
I. Increased pulmonary capillary wedge pressure
J. Increased left atrial pressure
